implementerProof.how: Re-drove the round-13 proof on the real surface, against a freshly seeded load-test stack (seed at migration 145, Dispatch built from 5a26d3ab). The implementer's claims held: a send queued past a lease publishes comment.created with the session's copy held as a fallback row, which is settled unpublished when the send lands; order holds through a sweep with real claim ageing; a Retry while attempt 1 is queued leaves one send.

proof.criterion: Review round 5 finding 1: a queued mention's claim does not keep comment.created deferred past about a minute.
proof.surface: POST /api/v1/issues/LGA-6/comments as a person on the local stack (listener at a 30 s round trip, so every send fails after its window); LGA-6 routed to the mentioned session:ses-x
proof.command: defer.sh head 40 (40 comments back to back on one lane; samples unpublished comment.created rows; counts ses-x's NATS copies)
proof.observed: Every comment.created was published within 63 s (p50 61 s) while its mention was still queued. All 40 attempts failed; 27 fallback rows were published and the rest got the route copy, so ses-x stores each comment exactly once. The same run on the pod before it was recreated gave the same numbers.
proof.negativeControl: defer.sh r12 40 with round 12's build 74779bec on the same database: publish delay max 188 s, p50 97 s, because each comment.created waited for its send to fail.

proof.criterion: Review round 5 finding 5: an API Retry while attempt 1 is queued leaves the recipient one copy, in either mode.
proof.surface: POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/deliveries as a person on the local stack (listener at 2 s; ses-y offers steer and aside)
proof.command: retry.sh head-aside aside; retry.sh head-steer steer (6 comments queue one lane; c6 is retried while its attempt 1 is pending and claimed)
proof.observed: Retry answers 201 with attempt 2 sent; attempt 1 is settled failed, 'not sent: a later attempt of this mention superseded it'; ses-y stores c6 once, in either mode, and c1-c5 once each.
proof.negativeControl: retry.sh r12-aside aside on round 12's build: attempt 1 (steer) and attempt 2 (aside) are both sent, and ses-y stores c6 twice.

proof.criterion: Review round 5 findings 3 and 4, and round 4's order rule: a recipient behind a lane backlog longer than a lease, with two live processes and the delivery sweep running, receives every comment once and in order.
proof.surface: Two envoy-dispatch processes on one database (38777 and 38778), listener at 2 s, 45 comments to ses-a
proof.command: steal.sh 45 (no route, session author); stealr.sh 45 (LGA-11 routed to ses-a); stealp.sh 45 (routed, person author)
proof.observed: The backlog settles about 187-190 s after the first post. In all three runs ses-a stores c1-c45 once each, in order, and process B sends nothing. In the person-authored routed run, 29 queued-past-a-lease attempts wrote fallback rows, all settled unpublished; comment.created was published within 65 s.
proof.negativeControl: Round 12 recorded the same steal.sh run on round 11's build delivering c33 before c30-c32.

proof.criterion: Review round 5 finding 2, and delivery through a kill and a rolling update: a stopping process hands its queued claims over at once, and every attempt is sent once.
proof.surface: The local stack: SIGKILL during shutdown (crash.sh), and SIGTERM with a successor process (rolling.sh)
proof.command: crash.sh r13person 1 150 (listener up); STOP_LISTENER=1 crash.sh r13down 1 170 (listener down after the restart); rolling.sh
proof.observed: Kill with the listener up: ses-a, ses-b and ses-c each get c1-c8 once; 8 fallback rows settled unpublished. Kill with the listener down: ses-a gets each comment once, from 8 published fallback rows. Rolling update: the old process releases its 27 queued claims at SIGTERM (27 pending and unclaimed at t+2 s; round 12 kept them claimed until they lapsed). The successor sends all 30 attempts once each to each session, in comment-creation order, including 4 comments committed during the drain; the last went out about 2 minutes after the SIGTERM.
proof.negativeControl: Round 12's rolling run on 74779bec showed the queued attempts still claimed (pending/unclaimed=false) until the lease lapsed.
